clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock held at 7:41 p.m. this week, with the underlying measurement inching from 461.3 to 461.4 minutes, a movement of one tenth of a minute. The shift was too small to change the public hour but registered as further confirmation of patterns already established in prior weeks.

grand_total_points.note: The aggregate clock movement was a tenth of a minute, reflecting broad but individually modest shifts across many traits rather than one dominant event.

delta_summary.moral_floor: Collapsing: character, ethics, restraint, truthfulness, and good faith all suffered breaches this week, with no offsetting improvement in any baseline trait.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The week did not open new categories of democratic harm but deepened existing ones across an unusually wide range of institutions, from local policing to federal statistics to public memory, while courts and civil society provided only partial, uneven resistance.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-six traits registered measurable movement this week, nearly all in the direction of erosion, spanning law enforcement, elections, civil service, immigration, and information control.

long_synopsis: Week 31 brought no single rupture, only accumulation across nearly every institution at once. Trump deployed National Guard troops and federal agents to seize control of Washington's police department, while Texas Republicans used surveillance and court orders to force through a Trump-requested gerrymander over Democratic resistance. Elsewhere, the administration pursued mail-voting restrictions tied to Putin's talking points, fired the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner over an unfavorable jobs report, revoked security clearances from three dozen intelligence officials, and expanded ideological vetting across immigration and citizenship systems. Courts offered partial resistance: blocking detention-facility expansion, restraining a Ten Commandments mandate, and releasing a wrongly deported man pending trial. The Democracy Clock barely moved, a tenth of a minute, because nothing here was unprecedented. Everything here was confirmed.
short_synopsis: Federal troops occupied Washington's streets, Texas forced through a gerrymander by coercion, and truth-telling institutions from labor statistics to intelligence absorbed loyalty purges. Courts pushed back at the margins. The clock barely moved because the week deepened patterns already in motion rather than opening new ones.
